title: [recoverability] the transcript archive masks credential values: every value the value collector places is replaced by [REDACTED:<name>] before a line is copied, in each of its forms; a pass that cannot have every value copies nothing and says why; restore puts a gone transcript back masked and never replaces a present one with masked copies
prompt:
Spawn, objective 175 [recoverability] (projects-47, 2026-11-14 16:16: the owner's D9, scoped by rev-f, the lead's decisions 11-14; reviewers rev-e, then cc-astra): the transcript archive masks credential values. Two commits: commit 1 moves the mask (pure move, the marker a parameter); commit 2 masks the archive. 179 (the archive.failed event and the archive_failed alert) follows it. R5 (2026-11-15, the lead and lead-mac): in the gate's sandbox, 047 and 048 failed closed on R4: the real collector, under the sandbox's empty HOME, said every credential file missing. So the sandbox gets an empty stand-in tool, and the binary honours a stand-in only there. R6 (cc-astra A81, the lead's design): SPAWN_GATE_SANDBOX=1 is a caller's word, not proof, so a stand-in is also refused when the Bridge's workspace root or transcripts directory is inside the account's home from the password database (where the live loop's are), unless that home is a tmpfs in the process's mounts (a gate's sandbox, where nothing live under it can be read); the live unit unsets both names; an accepted stand-in is said in one WARNING line naming its roots.

Line: core line 6 [recoverability].

Why. Spawn's transcript archive (`<root>/.transcripts`, crate::transcripts) is its own copy of every engine's transcript, kept for good: `--resume` and the scorecard read it, and transcripts are never deleted (the owner's rule). An engine that prints a credential it read (a `cat` of an env file, a URL with its password, a token in a tool's output) writes the value into its transcript, and the archive copies it in the clear, for good. The value collector (/usr/local/lib/spawn/redact/secret-values.py, the lead's) is the one list every value scan reads; nothing used it for the archive. Values may not pass through a file, a pipe or an argument (cc-astra A51), so the collector cannot hand them over: it says where each lies.

Order: the collector change (sync/obj-175/collector/: locate() and emit-locations.py, reviewed apart, installed by the lead as root with a hash check) is installed before 175 deploys. Without it, the Bridge has no mask, copies nothing, and says so every pass (fail closed); the archive falls behind until it is installed.

What changes:
Commit 1 (pure move; it builds and passes alone):
(1) crates/spawn-core/src/mask.rs: the mask's forms (as written, percent-encoded, base64, hex, JSON-escaped) and its span replacement move from crates/spawn-cli/src/mask.rs, with their four tests under the same names, and the marker becomes a parameter (`Mask::new(values, marker)`, `[<marker>:NAME]`); one new test, `the_marker_is_the_callers`. spawn-cli's mask.rs keeps read_values, `spawn mask` and `spawn mask-hook`, with `const MARKER: &str = "SECRET"`, so their output is unchanged. `pub mod mask;` in spawn-core's lib.rs, built always (not under the `testing` feature).
Commit 2:
(2) crates/spawn-core/src/port.rs: `TranscriptArchive` gains `source(agent, native, copy)` and `put_source(agent, native, copy, &CopySource)`: each copy's record, replaced whole and durably after each append. New port `ArchiveMask { fn mask(&self) -> Result<Arc<Mask>, String>; fn current(&self, mask: &Arc<Mask>) -> bool }`: the mask for this pass, or why not (paths only, never a value); and whether a mask it gave is still the one its sources give (R3).
(3) crates/spawn-core/src/transcripts.rs:
  - `CopySource { archive_length, source_offset, tail_sha256, masked }`. A masked copy is not the transcript's bytes, so its length no longer says where it stands in the transcript: the record does. `tail_sha256` is the sha256 of the transcript's 4096 bytes before `source_offset` (fewer at the start), the window today's byte comparison reads. A copy whose length is not its record's was cut by a crash between an append and its record: never appended to again, the next pass starts the next copy with the whole file. A copy with no record (made before 175) is the transcript's own bytes: its record is read as `{len, len, sha of its last 4096 bytes, false}`.
  - `archive_to(host, archive, masking: Option<Masking { mask, current }>, …)`: with a mask, only whole lines are copied (a line the engine is still writing waits for the next pass, so a value is never cut across two appends), each chunk through `Mask::bytes`, marker `REDACTED` (`ARCHIVE_MARKER`), and each append followed by its record. After the bytes are read and before each append, the mask is asked whether it is still current; if not, nothing more is copied that pass and the copy fails with MASK_CHANGED ("the credential files changed after the mask was built; copied on the next pass"), so no byte written after a rotation is masked by the mask from before it (R3: a rotation between the mask and the read). `Archived` gains `offset`, the transcript offset, which the Bridge keeps as ArchiveProgress.archived (first_line_ms reads the transcript at it). Without a mask, bytes are copied as before.
  - `restore(host, Option<Keeper { archive, mask: Result<Option<Masking>, &str> }>, …)`: a gone file is put back from the copies as they are, masked, and the latest copy's record becomes {that copy's length, the join's length, the sha256 of the join's last 4096 bytes, masked}: the put-back file is the transcript from then on, so the next pass goes on from its end in the same copy and never copies it whole again (R2, rev-e F1). A present file is replaced only when no copy is masked (by its record, or by holding `[REDACTED:` when its record is lost), so a present transcript is never replaced by masked bytes; otherwise `Restored::Left`. When the mask cannot be had, or went stale during restore's own copy (MASK_CHANGED), a present file is not archived first, so it is left. The Left warning says the three reasons.
(4) crates/spawn-core/src/bridge.rs: `Bridge::with_archive_mask(Arc<dyn ArchiveMask>)`. Each copy (copy_transcript, at the passes the transcript grew, at an execution's end, and an ended execution's retries) takes the mask first; without it the pass copies nothing and fails as a copy failure does today: warned when it changes ("the credential mask: …"), retried every pass, and the progress record's behind_ms says from when the archive lacks lines. ready_transcript passes the mask (or why not) to restore.
(5) crates/spawn-core/src/memory.rs, contract.rs: the in-memory archive keeps records; the shared archive contract checks them (read back, replaced, none for a copy not made).
(6) crates/spawn-host/src/transcripts.rs: LocalTranscriptArchive keeps records at `<root>-sources/<agent>/<native>.<copy>.json` beside `<root>-progress`, through the same temp-file-and-rename writer (now shared, `replace_whole`).
(7) crates/spawn-host/src/archive_mask.rs (new): `CollectorMask`. It runs `python3 -I -B <tool>` (/usr/local/lib/spawn/redact/emit-locations.py; 30 s limit; R5: another tool named by `SPAWN_ARCHIVE_LOCATIONS_TOOL` only inside a gate's sandbox, `SPAWN_GATE_SANDBOX=1`, else no tool runs and the mask is refused with "SPAWN_ARCHIVE_LOCATIONS_TOOL is honoured only in a gate's sandbox (SPAWN_GATE_SANDBOX=1): no location tool is run", and R6: refused too, marker and all, when a root it would mask for (the workspace root, the transcripts directory) is inside the account's home from /etc/passwd (never $HOME), unless that home is a tmpfs here, a gate's sandbox; an unknown home refuses; a root is judged where its symlinks lead. The limit, said plainly: the guarantee covers live roots inside the account's home, and a live root moved outside it would need the check extended (a unit test names the two live roots, ~/.local/share/spawn-rsi/ws and ~/.claude/projects, as refused, so a move shows there); a launcher with root, or one that binds the live tree elsewhere, is privileged tampering, which this does not stand against) and reads its JSON: per source a path, size, mtime_ns, device, inode and ctime_ns from the fd the collector read it through (R4, cc-astra A77: every field required, so an older collector's answer is refused and nothing copied); per value a path, a line (the file split as the collector's read() splits it: `\r\n`, a lone `\r`, `\n` and NUL) or a pointer of sorted-key and list indexes into a JSON source, a byte span, a transform (raw; pct: the span percent-decoded as Python's urllib.parse.unquote does, then `sub`; short: a short URL password's shape by its `form`, pair, b64 or word, from `user` and `pw` places and the collector's literal `pre`/`post` text) and a name. Missing or unreadable sources, a tool that refuses or answers no JSON, a source whose fstat (size, mtime_ns, device, inode and ctime_ns: R2, rev-e F2; R4) before and after the read is not the collector's stamp, so a same-size rewrite with its mtime set back is seen, also between the collector's answer and this read (R4, A77), and a place that is not there (no such line or pointer, a span past its text, a leaf that is not a string) are each an error naming the path, never a value. Every rule of what is a credential stays in the collector. The values go into the Mask in memory only; `Mask` has no Debug.
  - When the tool runs: the mask is kept with the stamps it was built from. Each call stats every source, every accepted-missing path (`accepted_paths`, absolute), every watched directory (`watch`: each source's own directory, each settings glob's base and each existing `.claude` under a glob, by mtime_ns, null when missing) and every probed path (`probe`: each workspace's `.claude`, by existence). It runs the tool again when a source's stamp (the same five fields, by stat) differs, an accepted path exists, a watched directory's mtime differs, a probed path's existence differs, the last run is 10 minutes old, or the last call failed. `current(mask)` is true only for the mask kept now and while none of these changed. So a rotation, a new older copy or a new workspace `.claude` that moves a stamp, a watched mtime or a probe is masked from the first pass that sees the change. A new file that leaves its directory's mtime equal (created in the same kernel clock tick as the last change before the baseline) is picked up when the mask is rebuilt: an archive attempt with a mask 10 minutes old or more discards it, and the installed collector must rebuild it before anything is copied. That is demand-driven, not a background scan: idle time, a failing collector and pass scheduling make it no strict wall-clock promise (the narrower guarantee accepted for the owner). With a stand-in (a gate's sandbox only) the rebuild runs the same stand-in and finds nothing new. A pass on the hot path costs stats, not a Python start (live: 88 stats, median 531 µs; the tool ran 11 times in 10 busy minutes, 60 ms each).
(8) crates/spawn-cli/src/runtime.rs: the loop's Bridge is built `.with_archive_mask(CollectorMask::from_env(&[workspace root, transcripts directory]))`; R6: when a stand-in is accepted the loop prints "spawn: WARNING: the transcript archive is masked by the stand-in location tool <tool> (SPAWN_GATE_SANDBOX=1), not the installed collector, for the roots <workspace root> and <transcripts>" (paths only; no event: a new host record shape is more than this needs).
(9) R7 (cc-astra A81 at 14:24: the roots were judged, not what is read and written below them): crates/spawn-host/src/beneath.rs (new). Every file below a root is opened from a descriptor of the root by openat2 with RESOLVE_BENEATH | RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS (rustix, no new crate, no unsafe): no component may be a symlink, nor a /proc magic link (/proc/<pid>/cwd, /proc/self/root: RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS implies RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS), and nothing resolves above the root (no `..` out of it, no absolute path). Directories are made one component at a time (mkdirat, then opened the same way); a rename, a link or an unlink is done between held directory descriptors (their last component is never followed); EAGAIN (a rename or a mount elsewhere raced the resolution) is tried again up to 32 times. A link met is an error "… goes through a link or leaves its root: not followed". A regular file with more than one hard link is refused the same way, before a byte is read or written ("<path> has <n> hard links: not followed"; rev-e's F1 on R7: `cp -al` of a live archive into scratch on the same filesystem makes every copy share its inode with live, and no walk sees the other name); nothing below a root is opened with O_TRUNC, and a temporary record is made new (O_EXCL) after removing any entry at its name.
- The archive (crates/spawn-host/src/transcripts.rs: the copies, `<root>-progress`, `<root>-sources`) always goes through it, the live loop's too, from the directory above the archive (the workspace root). One code path, the shared archive contract on it. A link below the workspace root (`.transcripts`, an agent's directory, a copy, a record) is from now on an error, on live as in a gate: nothing is copied, and the error goes where every archive error goes (the pass keeps behind_ms, says it in the loop's log, and tries again at the next pass; with 179 on top it is an `archive.failed` recorded once per change and 193's alert, cleared by the next pass that copies). On this host none of ws/.transcripts*, ~/.claude, ~/.claude/projects holds a link (counted 2026-11-15, read only). It needs openat2 (Linux 5.6 or later): an older kernel's ENOSYS, or a seccomp filter's EPERM in a container or sandbox, makes every archive open fail, loudly, the same way (rev-e's n1). On live this also refuses an archive moved by a link (the owner moving ws/.transcripts to another disk through a symlink must move the workspace root instead, or the archive copies nothing; rev-e's n2), and a backup that hard-links the archive's files (rsnapshot-style) would make every copy refused until its links are gone: on this host 0 of 224 files under ws/.transcripts have more than one link (the lead, read only, 2026-11-15).
- With a stand-in accepted, each root is pinned (Beneath::pinned): its deepest existing directory is opened, its canonical path must name that same directory (device and inode) and lie outside the account's home (unless the home is a tmpfs, as before); the device and inode are kept, and every later call reopens the directory and refuses when they differ, so a root swapped for a link after it was judged is refused. A root not made yet is judged at its deepest existing directory and the rest of it is walked like everything below (rev-e's n1 on R6). The archive uses the pinned workspace root (LocalTranscriptArchive::for_loop), and the terminal host reads, restores (write_new) and replaces (replace_grown) the engines' transcripts below the pinned projects root through it (TmuxHost::with_files_beneath).
- R8 (cc-astra A88 at 13:24 on R7: the terminal host chose its reader by the workspace prefix first, so with SPAWN_CLAUDE_PROJECTS inside the execution's workspace a native transcript was read by the workspace's reader, which neither holds the pin nor refuses a second hard link): TmuxHost::read_from now asks the pinned projects root first, as write_new and replace_grown already did; a path below it is read through it whatever other root also holds it, and only a path outside it goes to the workspace's reader or the native one. No layout falls back to a weaker rule: the pinned root, when it applies, always wins.
- The native side of a live loop is as before (O_NOFOLLOW on the last component only): ~/.claude is the user's own directory, and a user may keep it, or a project directory in it, behind their own links; a live loop reads the user's own transcripts whichever way the user laid them out, masked by the installed collector. A81 is about a loop with a stand-in mask (no real values masked) reaching live data through a link; that loop's native side is confined. So the user's own links on live are outside A81's scope, by decision (the lead, 2026-11-15).
- Not stood against, said plainly: a bind mount below a root (root or a user namespace), and privileged tampering.
- Cost (polled path: archive copies run all day): on a scratch archive of the live size (223 files, 634 MiB, 217 agents; sizes read from live, contents made up), one pass of copies() + a 200-byte append + a progress record per file, 10 rounds, release, twice each, host load 13-15 (sync/obj-175/r7-runs/bench): per copy, wall median 2.4 and 2.9 ms on 180b64ca, 2.8 and 3.1 ms with R7 (the fsyncs dominate); CPU median 554 and 578 us on 180b64ca, 630 and 652 us with R7 (about 75 us, 13 % more: the openat2 walk of three components per open). The read path the Bridge polls (copies(), progress()) is the same walk: no new read, no new syscall per poll beyond one openat2 per component.
Owner part: rsi/scenarios/175.sh (the contract). R5: scripts/rsi/gate.sh and scripts/blackbox/run-scenarios.sh set SPAWN_GATE_SANDBOX=1 and SPAWN_ARCHIVE_LOCATIONS_TOOL to an empty stand-in (no credential places) in the sandbox, unless a scenario names its own (175.sh, 196.sh), and the gate log says "| archive locations: an empty stand-in tool (no credential places) unless a scenario sets its own". Deploy, the loop units and live set neither. R6: deploy/systemd/spawn-loop.service says UnsetEnvironment=SPAWN_GATE_SANDBOX SPAWN_ARCHIVE_LOCATIONS_TOOL (after spawn.env and the manager's environment, so the live loop never inherits either), and scripts/blackbox/run-scenarios.sh says once "blackbox: archive locations: an empty stand-in tool (no credential places) unless a scenario sets its own (SPAWN_GATE_SANDBOX=1; a loop says WARNING when it uses one)".

Never changed: what the archive copies other than the masked values; old copies (nothing archived before 175 is rewritten: a value already archived stays until a separate, reviewed step); the transcript, which the archive reads and never writes except restore's write of a gone file; `spawn mask` and `spawn mask-hook` (marker SECRET); the progress records' shape.

Cost: per pass per execution whose transcript grew: one stat per credential source, accepted path, watched directory and probed path (88 on the live host: 18, 3, 14, 53; median 531 µs), and Mask::bytes over the new lines (forms in one pass, by first byte). The tool runs on a change or every 10 minutes per Bridge. No database read.

Files: crates/spawn-core/src/{mask.rs (new), lib.rs, port.rs, transcripts.rs, bridge.rs, memory.rs, contract.rs}, crates/spawn-core/Cargo.toml (sha2, a workspace dependency already), crates/spawn-host/src/{archive_mask.rs (new), archive_mask/tests.rs (new), transcripts.rs, lib.rs}, crates/spawn-host/Cargo.toml (serde, serde_json, workspace dependencies), crates/spawn-cli/src/{mask.rs, runtime.rs}, Cargo.lock; rsi/scenarios/175.sh, scripts/rsi/gate.sh, scripts/blackbox/run-scenarios.sh, deploy/systemd/spawn-loop.service (owner). 179 will touch bridge.rs and the alerts after 175.
Size (the lead: the move does not count; code and tests apart): commit 1 moves about 370 lines (spawn-cli mask.rs −371 +9, spawn-core mask.rs +419). Commit 2 adds 861 lines of code (43 of them the in-memory test backend's) and 628 of tests (+100 removed); R1 (rev-g's collector review: the split, the watch) adds 78 of code (−9) and 117 of tests (−2). R2 (rev-e's F1 and F2) adds 88 of code (−44) and 97 of tests (−2). R3 (the check after the read) adds 110 of code (−30) and 253 of tests (−3; 212 of them in spawn-core's tests/api.rs). e23c7b1c is cargo fmt only. R4 (cc-astra A77: the stamp's five fields) adds 16 of code (−2) and 60 of tests (−1). 175.sh is 889 lines.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/175.sh, black box. A real `spawn loop` runs one ephemeral worker on a fake engine; the credential files are made up and so is the location tool, a stand-in that prints places (raw, pct, a JSON pointer, a short password's pair) and stamps as emit-locations.py does, and lists a file it cannot read as unreadable. The engine, asked BB:SAY, writes one line with the values (an API token as written, percent-encoded and base64, a percent-encoded link's value, a JSON leaf, a database URL with a short password), cut inside the token into two writes 1.5 s apart.
(1) the archive holds `[REDACTED:spawn.env:API_TOKEN]` (3 times) and each other place's marker, no form of any value and no part of one; the transcript is byte for byte what the engine wrote.
(2) the token rotated and its file unreadable: a turn's lines are not copied (the archive unchanged 8 s on), the loop's log says why naming the file, no log holds a value; readable again, within 20 s the waiting lines are archived, masked.
(3) the transcript loses its head under the running engine; with the copies' records removed, a stop and resume leave the present file as it is.
(4) stopped, the transcript removed, resumed: it is put back masked, and the loop says it restored it. A turn after it is archived in the same copy: no new copy, and the archive (taken before the restore) grows by less than the restored file, so the restored bytes are not copied again.
(5) the token rotated back and its file unreadable, a turn, a stop and a resume: nothing is copied across the resume and the file is left; readable again, the waiting lines are archived masked.
(6) an older copy (spawn.env.bak, another value) appears beside the credential file, which is unchanged: a turn printing that value is archived masked within 20 s (the watched directory changed).
(7) a workspace under a watched base gains `.claude/creds.env` with another value: no watched directory changes, only the probed `.claude` appears; a turn printing that value is archived masked within 20 s.
(8) the credential file rewritten in place with another value of the same size, its mtime set back with `touch -r`: a turn printing that value is archived masked within 20 s (its ctime moved, so the tool runs again).
(9) R4 (A77): the tool answers, and right after it, before the Bridge reads the file, the file is rewritten in place to the same size with its mtime set back: the placed line now holds an ordinary value of the old value's length, and a new credential is on a line no place names. A turn printing the new credential is archived masked within 20 s: a source whose device, inode or ctime is not the tool's stamp is refused, and the tool run again.
(10) R5: the loop started again with the stand-in still named and no SPAWN_GATE_SANDBOX=1: a BB:SAY turn is not archived (the archive unchanged 8 s after it), and the loop's log says "SPAWN_ARCHIVE_LOCATIONS_TOOL is honoured only in a gate's sandbox"; the same with SPAWN_GATE_SANDBOX=0 (only `1` marks a gate). 175.sh sets SPAWN_GATE_SANDBOX=1 beside its stand-in for (1)-(9).
(12) R6: the loop that accepted 175.sh's stand-in says so in its log in one line naming the tool and its two roots (the WARNING line in (8)). A stand-in refused for roots inside the account's home is a unit test: a scenario never writes under the real home.
(13) R7: with the stand-in accepted, the loop started again with `<root>/.transcripts` a link to another directory: a BB:SAY turn writes nothing there, and the loop's log says "not followed". With the archive back, the engine's project directory under the transcripts root made a link to another directory (the engine writes through it): a BB:SAY turn is not archived (the archive unchanged 8 s after it), and the log says "not followed". Last, the agent's latest copy made a relative link to a file of the same bytes inside the workspace root (where the agents' own workspaces are): a BB:SAY turn writes nothing to that file, and the log says "not followed" (RESOLVE_BENEATH alone would follow a relative link that stays below the root; RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS refuses it, so an agent's files never stand for its copies). And the copy written last made a hard link to a file outside the workspace root: a BB:SAY turn writes nothing to it, and the log says "hard links: not followed". R8: the projects tree moved inside the teller's own workspace (SPAWN_CLAUDE_PROJECTS pointed there, a link left at the old path) and the teller's native transcript given a second name outside the workspace root: a BB:SAY turn is not archived (the archive unchanged), and the log says "hard links: not followed"; on R7 (c515373e) 175.sh exits 1 there. A link into the real home, a magic link, a swapped root and a missing root are unit tests. On R6 (180b64ca) 175.sh exits 1 at (13): "the archive wrote through a .transcripts that is a link".
On the base (main 6796e8c6) 175.sh exits 1 at (1): "the archive holds 3 of the value's 3 forms".

Tests (unit, made-up values only): spawn-core transcripts (whole lines and a value cut across passes; went on and replaced by the record; a cut copy and a copy without a record; restore masked, a present file left, the mask not had; a copy holding the marker), bridge (`the_archive_masks_values_and_copies_nothing_without_the_mask`), the archive contract; spawn-host archive_mask (each place kind read and masked; each place that does not hold is an error naming the source only; the mask built again on a stamp change, an accepted path, a watched directory's change or a probed path appearing, and on a same-size rotation with the old mtime; a mask is current until a source changes; lines split as the collector splits them; Python's percent-decoding; R5: a stand-in honoured only with SPAWN_GATE_SANDBOX=1, refused otherwise (unset, empty, 0, yes, "1 "), the installed tool when none is named; R6: `a_stand_in_is_refused_for_roots_inside_the_account_s_home_whatever_the_marker` (both variables set and a live-like root: refused, and not said accepted; a tmpfs home accepts; a root outside the home accepts; an unknown home refuses; a symlink judged where it leads), `the_live_loop_s_roots_refuse_a_stand_in` (the real account's ws and ~/.claude/projects), and the accepted stand-in is said (`stand_in()`)); spawn-core transcripts `a_restored_file_is_archived_on_in_the_same_copy`; spawn-core tests/api.rs (a rotating made-up mask through the Bridge): a mask that fails across a stop and a resume copies nothing, a rotation between a pass and a resume is masked with the new value, and a rotation between the mask and the read copies nothing that pass. R7: spawn-host beneath (`an_archive_whose_directory_links_into_the_home_appends_nothing_there`, pinned and unpinned; `an_agent_directory_or_a_copy_that_links_into_the_home_is_refused`; `a_magic_link_into_the_home_is_not_followed` (through /proc/self/root); `a_root_inside_the_home_is_refused_and_one_outside_is_pinned`; `a_root_swapped_for_a_link_after_it_was_pinned_is_refused`; `a_missing_root_is_pinned_at_its_deepest_directory_and_walked_below_it`; `files_below_a_root_are_made_listed_moved_linked_and_removed`; `a_link_that_stays_below_the_root_is_refused_too`; `a_copy_hard_linked_to_a_file_elsewhere_is_never_written_or_read` (pinned and unpinned); `a_transcript_hard_linked_to_a_file_elsewhere_is_not_read`; `a_project_directory_that_links_into_the_home_is_not_read_restored_or_replaced` (TmuxHost::with_files_beneath); `a_stand_in_mask_pins_its_roots_and_the_installed_one_pins_none`; `a_root_replaced_between_its_open_and_its_resolution_is_refused` (a cfg(test) step between the open and the canonicalize, so the check that both name one directory is seen without a race); `the_loop_s_archive_keeps_the_pin_of_its_workspace_root` (LocalTranscriptArchive::for_loop, which the runtime calls: a root swapped for a link after the pin writes nothing through it); R8: `a_native_transcript_inside_the_workspace_is_read_through_the_pinned_projects_root` (projects inside the workspace: a hard-linked native transcript refused, a plain one read, a workspace file still read by the workspace's reader, a projects root swapped after the pin refused)), every home a fake one in scratch. No test is renamed or dropped: commit 1's four moved tests keep their names (the gate compares names per module path).

Proof (rev-f, sync/obj-175/175-proof.txt).

Verified by (projects-47, after the collector is installed and 175 deploys): the guarantee is the narrower one lead-mac accepted for the owner: a new credential file missed by the mtime and probe checks is picked up when an archive attempt finds the mask 10 minutes old or more and the installed collector rebuilds it before copying (demand-driven, no zero-window claim, no wall-clock promise). Neither SPAWN_GATE_SANDBOX nor SPAWN_ARCHIVE_LOCATIONS_TOOL is set in spawn.env, the env files or the loop units, counted by name only (grep -c, no value printed); the loop's log has no "the credential mask" warning; a new copy under <root>/.transcripts that an engine wrote a credential into holds `[REDACTED:` and the collector's scan (secret-scan-files.py over the copies written since the deploy) finds no value; the progress records' behind_ms stay null.
